title: A Spectral Framework for Closed-Form Relative Density Estimation
claim: Debiased estimators converge faster and more accurately than regular ones, with measured scaling rates matching theory; the proposed estimators beat baselines.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: two line plots with error bars, then grouped bar chart
description: Three plots in a row. The left plot shows f-divergence against log2(n) for regular (blue), debiased (red), quantum (green) estimators and a black line for the true value. Regular and quantum curves decay slowly from above, while the red debiased curve with error bars hugs the true line. The center plot shows log(error) against log2(n) on a log-log scale, with solid curves and dotted power-law fits. The legend gives fitted exponents of 0.67, 0.58 and 0.70, and the red curve sits well below the others. The right plot is a grouped bar chart of relative estimation error at n = 512, 1024, 2048 and 4096. It compares KL*, KL, Pearson, variational, var.-square and KDE, and the KL and KL* bars are generally lowest. The eye goes first to the colored curves in the left plot.
caption: Left and Center: Comparison of quantum, regular, and debiased estimators of the KL divergence for q uniform on [0, 1] and p with a density having one square-integrable derivative, with a kernel equivalent to κ = 0 in Prop. 3, with a fixed n-dependent schedule for λ. Left: comparison of estimators with increasing n (mean and standard errors over 64 replications). Center: scaling laws with a power-law fit (decay proportional to n−σ with σ obtained from the data); the additive term in our bound is σ = 2/3. Right: Comparison of estimators of v and w (lower is better), with periodic data in [0, 1]2 mapped to a product of unit circles, with q uniform and p with independent components such that log(dp/dq) is a sum of a few cosines. We consider the ReLU kernel of order 1 [34], with m = 512 random features. We estimate from n observations and test on 1024 observations (for each method, we select the value of the hyperparameter that makes the error smallest on an independent validation set). KL corresponds to our new estimators of v and w, while KL∗corresponds to using −f ∗(v) = 1 −ev instead of w, which is expected to be better.
abstract: We propose a closed-form spectral framework for relative log-density estimation in linearly parameterized probabilistic models, including unnormalized and conditional models. This is achieved by representing the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence as an integral of weighted chi-squared divergences, converting KL estimation into a family of least-squares problems. We derive an explicit spectral formula based only on first- and second-order feature moments, yielding closed-form estimators of both divergences and log-density potentials for fixed features. The framework extends to a broad class of $f$-divergences and can be combined with kernelization or feature learning with neural networks (with then only a closed form for the last layer). We prove convergence guarantees for the resulting estimators and empirically compare them on synthetic data with optimization-based variational formulations, including logistic and softmax regression for normalized conditional models.
